faq: What if a user loses their phone?
They can use a backup code, or contact support for a careful reset. We design the recovery so it is safe, and does not let a stranger talk their way in.
Does it work with Google Authenticator?
Yes. We use the standard time-based codes, so Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password and similar apps all work.
Will text message codes be included?
Not by default. Text codes are weaker and need a paid SMS service. Authenticator apps are safer. If you still need text, we can quote it separately.
Can I add it to an app that uses a login service?
Often yes. Auth0, Clerk, Firebase and others include two-step options. We turn those on if they fit, and build it ourselves only when it makes sense for you.

desc:
Two-factor authentication for SaaS accounts adds a second step at login, usually a short code from an authenticator app. Ecom Swift LLC builds the set-up screen, backup codes and recovery path in your own app, so extra safety never locks people out.

## What is two-step login?

Two-step login, also called two-factor authentication or 2FA, asks for something in addition to a password. The most common choice is a six-digit code from an authenticator app on the user's phone, which changes every few moments. A stolen password alone is then no longer enough to enter the account.

It can also use email codes, security keys or passkeys, depending on what you want to support.

## Why a password alone falls short

Passwords get reused, guessed, phished and leaked. A person who uses the same password on several sites is exposed whenever any one of them is breached. For ordinary accounts that may be an acceptable risk. For admins, owners and customers who hold valuable data, it often is not.

The risk grows with the power of the account. One compromised admin can read every customer's data, so the people with the most access should carry the strongest protection.

## How two-step login affects trust and incidents

A second step works because it breaks the link between a leaked password and a break-in. An attacker who holds only the password still lacks the code that sits on the owner's phone. That removes one of the most common routes into accounts.

It also helps with sales. Business customers ask whether you offer it, and some require it for staff who use your product. Offering it, and letting an admin require it for chosen roles, answers the question. We cannot promise that no account will ever be taken over, because attackers have other methods, but the feature raises the effort needed.

## What a great two-step setup includes

- A set-up screen with a QR code and a manual key.
- A six-digit code field at login with clear error messages.
- Codes verified on the server, with limits on wrong attempts.
- A switch to turn it on and off in security settings.
- Ten one-use backup codes shown once and easy to download.
- A rule to require it for owners, admins or any chosen role.
- A trusted device option so people are not asked on every visit.
- An email notice when two-step login is turned off.
- A recovery path for a lost phone that does not rely on guesswork.
- An admin tool to reset a user's second step after checking identity.

## What we do

We first agree who should use it and how strict you want to be. Then we build the set-up flow, the login challenge and the server checks, and we connect them to your current login so nothing else changes for people who have not enabled it.

We pay special attention to recovery, because that is where most designs fail. We test a lost phone, a used backup code, a changed device and an admin reset. The aim is that a legitimate user can always get back in, and an attacker cannot talk their way past the step.

The Basic package gives optional authenticator app codes with QR set-up. Standard adds backup codes, role-based requirements, trusted devices, a notice email and recovery steps. Premium adds email codes, security keys and passkeys, an admin reset tool, an event log and a handover call.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Require it first for admins and owners.
- Give backup codes at the moment of set-up.
- Notify the user when the second step is changed.
- Limit wrong code attempts.
- Test the lost-phone path before launch.

**Avoid:**
- Making it mandatory with no recovery route.
- Storing the secret key in a readable log.
- Letting support turn it off without checking identity.
- Treating email codes as equal to an authenticator app.
- Showing backup codes again after the first time.

## Who this is for

It suits a SaaS product whose admins handle sensitive customer data. It also fits a business whose larger customers have asked for stronger login, or a team that has seen an account taken over and wants to reduce the chance of a repeat. Products that store financial, health or private business information are natural candidates.

## What we need from you

Tell us which roles should use it and how strict you want to be. We need collaborator or developer access to the project and a staging environment, and a test account for each role. We never need passwords. If your login runs through an outside service, share its name so we can check how the second step fits with it.
